title: Efficacy and Safety of a Brief Transdiagnostic Cognitive Behavioral Intervention: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
This study represents a randomized controlled trial on the efficacy and safety of a brief cognitive behavioral intervention for patients with different psychological diagnoses (depression and anxiety disorders).

In Germany, patients have to wait five month on average to receive outpatient psychotherapy. Transdiagnostic therapy in groups is an effective opportunity to shorten these waiting periods. However, manualized transdiagnostic interventions usually include 12 to 16 sessions. Shorter interventions are needed to bridge waiting periods. 

Theresefore, the present study aims at evaluating the efficacy of a brief five session transdiagnostic cognitive-behavioral intervention to reduce psychological distress in patients with depression and anxiety disorders. In addition, the efficacy of the intervention to reduce disorder specific symptoms (depression and anxiety symptoms) as well as to improve emotion regulation and mindfulness is investigated. Patients will randomly be allocated to the intervention group or a waiting-list control group. Symtoms will be assessed at baseline (T1), after completion of the intervention (T2) and at follow-up (T3).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- fluent in spoken and written German
- the presence of one of the following ICD-10 diagnosis: F32, F33, F34.1, F40 (exclusion: F40.2, specific phobia), F41
Exclusion criteria:
- current psychotherapeutic treatment
- regular use of benzodiazepines
- change in psychopharmacological medication less than 4 weeks ago
- acute suicidality
- current addiction disorder (alcohol and/or drugs)
- current psychosis
- current (hypo)mania (ICD-10: F30) or bipolar affective dirsorder (ICD-10: F31)
- current pregnany or breastfeeding period
